verses.verse:
सकारेण शरीरः स्याद् धकारो भवेत्।
नकारेण स्मृतः प्राणः साधना त्रिगुणात्मिका।६०।
verses.text: By the syllable sa the body is meant; dha [stands for concentration]; by na the life-breath is understood: [so] sādhanā has the nature of the three guṇas.

commentary.text: Broadly, the meaning of sādhanā is the activity that leads from ignorance towards knowledge. Even so, here the author's own intent is given, which is set out in this śloka on the basis of scientific truth. Until body, mind and prāṇa (life-breath) are brought in one direction and one sets out from comfort towards discomfort, there can be no sādhanā of any subject. So, (sa) for śarīra (body), dha for dhāraṇā (concentration) and na for prāṇa: thus, by including body, mind and prāṇa in sādhanā, sādhanā has been described as having the three guṇas, sattva, rajas and tamas.

subsection.title: Here Begins the Section on Practice
